q: Partition Equal Subset Sum is equivalent to…
options: Finding a subset that sums to total / 2
why: If one half sums to total / 2, the rest does too.

q: Why iterate capacity DOWNWARD in 0/1 knapsack?
options: So can[s − x] still refers to the previous round and x isn't used twice
why: Going upward would read values already updated with x in this round.

q: Coin Change II (count combinations): which loop is outer?
why: Coins outer builds each combination in one fixed coin order; amounts outer counts permutations.

q: Target Sum: nums = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1], target = 3. Subset sum you count?
Why is subset-sum DP called pseudo-polynomial?
options: Its cost depends on the numeric value of the target, not just the input length
why: A target of 10⁹ makes the table huge even for a short list.
The total is 7, which is odd: no equal split.
